name: Data Analyzer: A cache folder that is a shortcut to another folder is refused
objective: Proves the cache does not write through a symbolic link planted by someone else; it uses a private fallback folder and still works.
precondition: Test harness with a temporary folder for the dictionary cache and a made-up 32-character session identifier. Linux/macOS file permissions are used. No network.

steps.action: Make the cache base folder a symbolic link to another folder, then store and read back one item.
steps.expected: The item round-trips; the cache folder in use is not a link and is not the planted one; the other folder stays empty; the fallback folder permits no group or other access.

name: Data Analyzer: A cache folder open to other users is refused
objective: Proves a world-writable cache folder is not used.
precondition: Test harness with a temporary folder for the dictionary cache and a made-up 32-character session identifier. Linux/macOS file permissions are used. No network.

steps.action: Create a cache folder with full permissions for everyone, then store and read back one item.
steps.expected: The item round-trips, the folder in use differs from the open one, and the open folder stays empty.

name: Data Analyzer: A per-session cache folder that is a shortcut is refused
objective: Proves a link planted in place of the session folder is not followed.
precondition: Test harness with a temporary folder for the dictionary cache and a made-up 32-character session identifier. Linux/macOS file permissions are used. No network.

steps.action: Make the session sub-folder a symbolic link to another private folder, then store and read back one item.
steps.expected: The item round-trips, a different folder is used, and the link target stays empty.

name: Data Analyzer: A properly private cache folder is used normally
objective: Proves the safety checks do not reject a good folder.
precondition: Test harness with a temporary folder for the dictionary cache and a made-up 32-character session identifier. Linux/macOS file permissions are used. No network.

steps.action: Create the cache on a new folder and store and read back one item.
steps.expected: The item round-trips and the folder in use is the one requested.

name: Data Analyzer: A cache entry that is a shortcut to another file is neither read nor overwritten
objective: Proves a planted link cannot leak or overwrite another file.
precondition: Test harness with a temporary folder for the dictionary cache and a made-up 32-character session identifier. Linux/macOS file permissions are used. No network.

steps.action: Plant a link for one cache entry pointing at a file containing '{"stolen": true}' and read the entry.
steps.expected: The read gives nothing (no data returned).

steps.action: Plant the link again, then store {fresh: 1} and read it back.
steps.expected: The target file still holds the original text; the entry reads back as {fresh: 1}.

name: Data Analyzer: A cache entry that is a special file (named pipe) is refused without hanging
objective: Proves a special file in the cache cannot make the page freeze. The test only checks that reading returns nothing and that writing returns; it asserts nothing about the written result.
precondition: Test harness with a temporary folder for the dictionary cache and a made-up 32-character session identifier. Linux/macOS file permissions are used. No network.

steps.action: Create a named pipe in place of an entry, read it, then try to store an item.
steps.expected: The read returns nothing and neither call hangs or crashes (no further check).

name: Data Analyzer: A normal small PDF is read through the separate child process
objective: Proves the real isolated PDF reader works end to end for ordinary files.
precondition: Test harness with a small PDF built in memory from made-up text. No network and no AI model.

steps.action: Extract text and page count from a 2-page PDF.
steps.expected: Text is 'one', new line, 'two', new line; page count is 2.

name: Data Analyzer: A PDF with too much text is refused
objective: Proves the text-size limit is enforced through the child process.
precondition: Test harness with a small PDF built in memory from made-up text. No network and no AI model.

steps.action: Extract text from a 2-page PDF of 600 characters per page with a 1000-character limit.
steps.expected: A 'too large' error whose message mentions 'characters'.

name: Data Analyzer: A PDF with too many pages is refused and the message gives the counts
objective: Proves the page limit is enforced and the message says the actual and allowed number.
precondition: Test harness with a small PDF built in memory from made-up text. No network and no AI model.

steps.action: Extract text from a 4-page PDF with a limit of 3 pages.
steps.expected: A 'too large' error matching '4 pages; the limit is 3'.

name: Data Analyzer: A stuck PDF reader is stopped at the time limit
objective: Proves a PDF that makes the reader hang cannot freeze the page.
precondition: Test harness with a small PDF built in memory from made-up text. No network and no AI model. In the test, the PDF reading helper process is replaced by a tiny script: it sleeps for 60 seconds. Time limit set to 1 second.

steps.action: Extract text from a PDF while the helper hangs.
steps.expected: A 'too large' error saying it 'took too long', and the whole call returns in under 10 seconds.

name: Data Analyzer: A PDF reader that crashes or returns nonsense is refused
objective: Proves every bad outcome from the helper gives a clean error, not a crash or wrong text. Runs for 6 scripts.
precondition: Test harness with a small PDF built in memory from made-up text. No network and no AI model. In the test, the PDF reading helper process is replaced by a tiny script: each one of six scripts.

steps.action: Extract text with the helper replaced in turn by: exit with an error code; print non-JSON text; kill itself; report 'ok' without text; report an unknown status; do nothing.
steps.expected: Every case raises the 'too large' error.

name: Data Analyzer: A PDF reader that outputs far too much text is refused
objective: Proves the output size cap. The test checks that an error is raised; it does not directly check that the child process was stopped.
precondition: Test harness with a small PDF built in memory from made-up text. No network and no AI model. In the test, the PDF reading helper process is replaced by a tiny script: it prints 5 million characters.

name: Data Analyzer: The PDF reader process cannot see API keys or Azure settings
objective: Proves secrets in the environment are not passed to the process that opens untrusted PDFs.
precondition: Test harness with a small PDF built in memory from made-up text. No network and no AI model. A made-up API key and Azure address are set. In the test, the PDF reading helper process is replaced by a tiny script: it lists any environment variable starting with DATA_ANALYZER, AZURE or LLM_ and returns the list as text.

steps.action: Extract text and look at the returned list.
steps.data: Variables DATA_ANALYZER_API_KEY and AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT set in the test
steps.expected: The returned text is exactly 'leaked:' with nothing after it.

name: Data Analyzer: The PDF reader program does not load the web page code
objective: Proves the child process stays minimal and does not pull in the app or its libraries.
precondition: Test harness with a small PDF built in memory from made-up text. No network and no AI model.

steps.action: Load the reader program in a fresh Python process and check which modules are loaded.
steps.expected: The answer is False: neither the web page module nor Streamlit is loaded.

name: Data Analyzer: The PDF reader's memory ceiling really stops a huge allocation (Linux only)
objective: Proves the memory limit works. This test is SKIPPED on macOS and any non-Linux system because the limit is not enforced there; it runs only in the Linux container.
precondition: Linux only. A fresh Python process with the reader's memory limit set to 100 MB.

steps.action: Try to allocate 1 GB after applying the limit.
steps.expected: The program prints 'refused' (a memory error), not 'allocated'. On macOS the test is skipped and records nothing.

name: Data Analyzer: The memory limit helper never crashes
objective: Proves that on any system the helper returns yes/no instead of an error. It accepts either answer, so it checks only that nothing is raised.
precondition: Reader program loaded directly in the test process.

steps.expected: The result is True or False; no error is raised.
